transcript_coverage.statement: The reasoning record of this book is thin and must be read as such. Of the 41 attempts that produced this corpus (3 writers, 8 primaries, 4 peers, 3 boss attempts, 4 authors, 6 order-execution attempts, 5 spot lanes, 2 cure attempts, 1 fix attempt, 2 postchecks, 3 sidecars), six left a runtime transcript that still exists (two authors, one order-execution author, two primaries, one boss); 35 left none, either because the runtime never wrote one or because it deleted the file before it was mirrored, and one manifest-recorded transcript of 80 bytes (attempt unattributed) is gone with only its digest surviving. Even the six surviving transcripts carry no chain of thought: every thinking block in them is an empty string with a signature, so what was audited is actions, tool arguments, tool results, file writes and narration, not reasoning. The 9,778,043 bytes the transcript-audit stage processed include 3,890,665 bytes belonging to five attempts of the previous, already-closed book; 5,887,378 bytes belong to this book. The reconciliation tool I ran reports GREEN (11 transcripts assigned across 4 disjoint slices equal the manifest's 11, every packet reports exactly its assigned files, bytes processed equal bytes assigned, close-read bytes never exceed processed bytes). Consequences for this verdict: everything written by a subagent (deliverables, final messages, receipts) was auditable and was audited against bytes; claim-versus-act divergence could be tested for six attempts of 41, and in those six every one showed at least one undisclosed departure from its launch rules, so a reader must NOT infer that the 35 untranscribed attempts behaved better, only that their outputs were independently verified from bytes. A reader must also not infer that the owner's directive to audit chain of thought has been met for this book; it has been met for zero attempts, and the runtime, not any agent, is the cause.

escalation.question: OW-6c reserves an end-of-campaign decision on re-checking 'all work and all chain of thought'. As of this book, chain of thought is unrecoverable for the 24 books closed before this session (no transcripts exist) and for 35 of this book's 41 attempts (never written or deleted by the runtime); the six surviving transcripts contain actions, not reasoning (every thinking block is empty). Should OW-6c be re-scoped NOW, before 41 more books accrue under the same capture, and should agent-written reasoning records be adopted from the next book as the durable substitute? Two related rulings are made below without the owner and are reported for information; one fact (the orchestrator's model) is put to the owner for a one-line confirmation.
escalation.recommendation: Re-scope OW-6c now to three tiers: (a) all work products - corpora, packets, receipts, logs - which are complete and re-checkable for every book; (b) captured transcripts where they exist, with the manifest per book stating which attempts have one; (c) from the next book, a short agent-written reasoning record per attempt (what was verified from bytes, what was changed, what is still doubted), ordered by every brief and audited against the artifacts. State plainly in the OW-6c packet that the chain of thought of the 24 closed books and of most of this book's attempts does not exist and cannot be recovered. Keep the mirror at every wave landing and the 60-second snapshot during waves. Confirm the orchestrator's model so the receipt record can be corrected.
escalation.recommendation_reason: The option set the owner reserved is already half-impossible, and a decision at book 66 changes nothing about what is captured, whereas a decision now changes what is captured for 41 books. The transcript audit proved its value precisely where transcripts existed (undisclosed breaches found only there), so the substitute should be adopted, not the goal abandoned. Reasoning records are cheap, durable and auditable, but they are self-reports and must never be presented to the owner as chain of thought. The runtime's failure to write transcripts is outside any agent's control, so a pause to engineer full capture would cost continuity and buy little.

rulings_made_without_the_owner.question_put: EVIDENCE RETENTION - is the residual mirror window acceptable for the remaining 41 books or does closing it need an owner decision about cost and storage?
rulings_made_without_the_owner.ruling: Does not need the owner. The window between a wave landing and the mirror run is now bounded by a mirror at every landing plus a 60-second snapshot loop during waves, both already in use, at negligible storage (about 10 MB for this book). The dominant loss - transcripts never written by the runtime, about 85 percent of attempts here - is not a cadence problem and no mirror cadence recovers it; spending owner attention on the window would address the smaller loss. Order: keep both mechanisms on every wave, record per-attempt transcript presence in every receipt, and adopt the reasoning record as above pending the owner's answer to the question.
